doc.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Juilliard rejection and Janet Schenck at Manhattan School
summary: Katz is turned away at Juilliard but admitted to Manhattan School by Janet Schenck; Teddy Wilson teaches jazz piano at Juilliard.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: teaching a course of jazz piano at Juilliard. The only one. It wasn’t a course it was like three or four guys that you’d go in and you’d play for him and it was almost like individual lessons with just a few. And I guess he was there because of his name, I don’t know, because there was no jazz program. And I always wondered how do guys like Miles go there? He didn’t study —

I just don’t know how he got in. Because I didn’t get in, I applied to Juilliard and I had to play a rigid classical repertoire, and they said well you play okay but this is for really serious classical advanced students and we have too many now so I was sort of discouraged. But I applied to Manhattan. This is interesting because I went in there and they had similar entrance requirements, this little old lady named Janet Schenck who was the head of the school, this classical maven and she was a wealthy social activist. It started out as a settlement house, the Manhattan School of Music, and she was this incredible character. So she says, I started to play my classical thing, I got halfway through a Mozart sonata and she said, “Oh that’s nice but it says here that you play jazz music. Would you play something for me?” So I don’t know what I played. She says, “You’ll be fine.”
